key_insight: EDEN is a large, freely available Italian emergency department clinical-notes corpus with both full-text data and a structured expert-annotated subset for information extraction.
clinical_relevance: It can support development and evaluation of large language models for real emergency-care documentation tasks in Italian, especially extracting structured clinical facts from notes.
method: Collected ~4 million fully anonymized ED notes from Italian hospitals.
Manually annotated ~6,000 notes with a 132-item CRF for dyspnea and loss of consciousness.
Defined mixed-value labels (numeric, categorical, binary) and iteratively refined the scheme with clinicians.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports corpus statistics, annotation details, and zero-shot baseline results from Gemma-27B and MedGemma-27B on the CRF-filling benchmark.
watch_item: The annotated subset is relatively small and highly imbalanced, so model performance may not generalize evenly across all CRF items or clinical scenarios.
paper_title: EDEN: A Large-Scale Corpus of Clinical Notes for Italian
